title: Exploring Text Specific and Blackbox Fairness Algorithms in Multimodal Clinical NLP
notes: Two-column PDF extraction interleaves columns, so quotes are single-line substrings. Section 4.1 states the sensitive groups are ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White, other), biological sex (male/female) and insurance type (government, medicare, medicaid, self-pay, private, unknown); the quote captures only the ethnicity clause because column interleaving prevents a longer verbatim span. audits_selection coded 'no': the paper filters heavily (drops ICU stays with no linked notes and notes with causal leakage) and reports the retained cohort's demographic distribution in Table 1 / Appendix A.4, but never compares that composition to the pre-filter Harutyunyan et al. cohort or any external denominator. Appendix Table 4's caption acknowledges results are not comparable to Harutyunyan 'since we ignore patients without any clinical notes' — a total-count-level caveat with no demographic breakdown, so it does not qualify even under the permissive reading. null_attribute_handling coded separate_category because an explicit UNKNOWN insurance group is retained and analysed (994 train / 192 test); ethnicity has an 'OTHER' bucket the authors describe as arising from poorly-defined labels, and the race-debiasing step excludes 'other'.

title: An exploratory data analysis: the performance differences of a medical code prediction system on different demographic groups
notes: Text is a two-column PDF extraction in which left- and right-column text share the same physical line, so quotes are deliberately short single-line fragments. Paper reports micro/macro/sample F1 and FNR/FPR separately for gender, age, ethnicity and insurance groups (Tables 3-4), with Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney tests between groups, so audits_model_on_pool = yes. Cohort is the MIMIC-III 50 subset with Mullenbach et al. splits, plus collapsing of rare ethnicity/insurance values into 'OTHER'. audits_selection = no: Table 1 and the statement that the data 'includes more White patients than patients from other ethnic groups' describe the composition of the final dataset only; there is no pre-selection or external denominator (no comparison to full MIMIC-III, to Beth Israel catchment, or to census). Grep over the file for missing/unknown/not reported/declined/imputation/complete case returned zero hits, hence not_mentioned.

title: Promoting Fairness in Classification of Quality of Medical Evidence
notes: Two-column PDF text; quotes are single-line substrings because sentences are interleaved with the adjacent column. Data are Cochrane systematic-review/clinical-trial records, and the protected attribute is the SEX OF STUDY PARTICIPANTS (plus 'medical area', which is not a demographic/SES attribute so it is not listed in protected_attributes). Included because TPR is reported separately per Sex group (Figure 1, Table 7). audits_selection coded no: the paper reports only within-dataset group shares (13-22% Female, 1-2% Male in Tables A1/A3) and notes 'for some groups, there is comparatively less research available', with no pre-selection denominator or retention rate. null_attribute_handling coded unclear: the paper says protected-annotation availability varies and that they therefore build different dataset versions per attribute, but never states what happens to records lacking the annotation; grep for missing/unknown/imputation/complete case found no relevant hits.

title: When Demographic Sensitivity Isn’t What It Seems: Baseline-Aware Counterfactual Audits for Clinical NLP
notes: HARD CASE: borderline on both inclusion and audits_selection. Inclusion: the 'groups' are not patient subgroups but counterfactual perturbation arms (age swap vs sex swap); Table 3/Table 5 report urgency-label and action change rates separately per demographic attribute, which I treated as a disaggregated fairness metric by attribute (counterfactual_consistency). audits_selection: Tables 5 and 7 report the number of 'valid pairs'/'valid structured outputs retained' per perturbation condition (e.g. gemini age swap 15 vs sex swap 16 vs base 19), i.e. differential parse-failure retention across demographic perturbation arms. I coded 'no' because these are prompt conditions, not protected-attribute groups of patients, and the paper never evaluates the parse filter for differential retention or compares against a pre-selection denominator. Cohort is 12 author-constructed synthetic EHR-style vignettes; per the rules, author sampling/curation counts as filtering. Demographics are assigned by construction, so no missing-attribute problem arises; grep for missing/unknown/imputation/complete case returned nothing.

title: CheXclusion: Fairness gaps in deep chest X-ray classifiers
notes: Model audit only. Composition figures (67.6% White, 8.98% Medicaid) are given for the final cohort with no pre-selection or external denominator, so both selection fields are 'no'. null_attribute_handling coded 'drops' on a judgement call: the only statement about records lacking race/insurance is the parenthetical '(excluding around 100,000 images)'; the words 'missing'/'unknown' never appear in the paper (searched).

title: Hurtful Words: Quantifying Biases in Clinical Contextual Word Embeddings
notes: Heavily filtered cohort (Harutyunyan-style cohort selection, restriction to Nursing/Nursing-other/Physician note types, dropping outpatient notes because they cannot be linked to insurance status, dropping patients with no qualifying note in the first 48h). The paper reports the retained cohort's demographic composition as raw percentages but supplies no pre-selection denominator and makes no comparison to the full MIMIC-III population or any census figure, so both the strict and permissive selection-audit codes are 'no'. Note that the 'unknown' language/ethnicity records and the small self-pay and government insurance groups are dropped, which is itself an unaudited second filter operating on protected attributes; the authors do not report how large those dropped groups are.

title: Assessing Social Determinants-Related Performance Bias of Machine Learning Models: A case of Hyperchloremia Prediction in ICU Population
notes: Clear model audit: bootstrapped AUC per race/gender/insurance subgroup with permutation tests against the full-test-set baseline (Table 3). Cohort filtering is explicit (age >=18, no re-admissions, no day-1 hyperchloremia, non-missing day-1 chloride) and reduces 'over 40,000 ICU encounters' in MIMIC-III to 33,330, but only total counts are given - no demographic breakdown of who was excluded and no comparison to the parent database or an external population - so both audits_selection and audits_selection_literal are no. Race missingness (12.8%) is reported but the paper never states what was done with those encounters (they simply do not appear in the four race subgroups), so coded reports_only rather than drops.

title: A Transformer-Based Deep Learning Approach for Fairly Predicting Post-Liver Transplant Risk Factors
notes: OPTN/UNOS registry 1987-2018. Table 3 reports Demographic Parity Difference and Equalized Odds Difference for each of five tasks stratified by age, gender and race/ethnicity; Figure 4 reports outcome (risk-factor) rates per subgroup. cohort_is_filtered coded yes because the analysis cohort is restricted to post-transplant recipients drawn from a registry that also covers waiting-list registrations; this is the only narrowing the paper describes and no exclusion/flow counts are given. audits_selection coded no: Table 1 is a plain final-cohort demographic description with no pre-selection denominator, and no comparison of included vs excluded patients appears anywhere. null_attribute_handling coded unclear: MICE is stated for 'missing values and outliers' generally, but the paper never says whether the stratifying attributes (gender, age, race/ethnicity) had missing values or whether those specifically were imputed; Table 1 does show an 'Unknown' category (26.30%) for EDUCATION, which is not one of the attributes used for the fairness analysis.

title: Auditing ICU Readmission Rates in an Clinical Database: An Analysis of Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes
notes: HARD CASE: the paper's 'Equal Parity' / 'Proportional Parity' language repeatedly says groups are 'underrepresented in the selected set' (e.g. Medicaid 0.16X, Female 0.53X, Black 0.14X). In context 'selected set' means the set of patients the MODEL predicts positive (PPR/PPGR), i.e. a demographic-parity model metric, NOT the cohort-selection step; coded audits_selection=no. Second judgement call on audits_selection_literal: Section IV.A reports MIMIC-III parent-database demographics (~55% male, ~69% White) and Table III separately reports final-cohort group size ratios (White 0.69, Black 0.11), but the authors never draw the comparison, so literal=no; the conclusion's representativeness caveat cites no figure. Missingness: the only 'unknown' hit describes MIMIC insurance categories ('other/unknown'), not a handling statement, and the analysed insurance groups omit unknown. The source file is two-column text merged line-by-line, so every quote is a single-line substring. Cohort: 6.5K examples after filtering (adults, first ICU stay, excluding in-hospital deaths and inter-unit transfers).

title: Unmasking Parkinson's Disease with Smile: An AI-enabled Screening Framework
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection_literal. Strict audits_selection = no: 827 of 1059 participants were retained (those with all three expression videos) and participants missing ethnicity were dropped from subgroup analyses, but the paper never compares the composition or retention rate of the retained cohort against the pre-filter cohort. For the permissive reading I coded yes on the strength of the Supplementary Table 7 caption, which explains the clinic cohort's 97.3% white composition by reference to the Rochester catchment population - an explicit comparison of cohort composition to a catchment-population referent, which the rules list as qualifying. Two weaker candidates I did NOT rely on: the abstract/intro statement 'Testing the system on external cohorts in Bangladesh (representing South-East Asia, 8.5% of global population) and the United States (representing Northern America, 4.7% of global population)' (external figures, but about region coverage rather than cohort composition), and 'the participants were dominated by U.S. residents (754 out of 827, 91.2%)' (internal proportion, no external referent). If the coder disagrees on the catchment-caption reading, this field flips to no.

title: Large Language Models to Identify Social Determinants of Health in Electronic Health Records
notes: The by-group metric is a counterfactual consistency rate measured on GPT4-generated synthetic sentences with race/ethnicity and gender descriptors injected, not on the real patient cohort; I still coded audits_model_on_pool 'yes' because a disparity metric is reported by demographic descriptor. Note selection is heavily filtered (>=150 tokens, section requirements, patients with at least one social work note), but the paper never breaks retention down by group. The 'predominantly white population' statement cites no external figure, so audits_selection_literal stays 'no'.

title: On the notion of Hallucinations from the lens of Bias and Validity in Synthetic CXR Images
notes: Very short workshop-style paper. Included because it reports TPR by intersectional gender-x-ethnicity subgroup on a defined MIMIC-CXR subset (18,200 images) for both real and synthetic images. The filtering sentence is oddly worded ('filtering out scans with consistent demographic information') and probably means inconsistent, but I coded cohort_is_filtered=yes on the plain text since it plus 'retaining one scan per patient' unambiguously describes narrowing MIMIC-CXR down to 18,200 samples. No pre-filter demographic denominator is reported anywhere, so both selection-audit codes are 'no'. The one comparative claim — that the Hispanic female subgroup performs worse 'despite its larger sample size' — is a within-cohort observation with no external referent. A full-file grep for missing / unknown / not reported / declined / imputation / complete case returned zero hits, hence not_mentioned.

title: FMBench: Benchmarking Fairness in Multimodal Large Language Models on Medical Tasks
notes: Benchmark paper: GREEN scores and lexical scores are reported per demographic group for eight MLLMs (Tables 4-5), plus the new FAP metric (weighted mean performance minus weighted deviation across groups), so audits_model_on_pool = yes and fairness_metrics is coded 'other' because FAP/GREEN-by-group do not map onto the listed labels. cohort_is_filtered = yes on the benchmark-construction clause of the rules: the authors built FMBench from the single-institution Harvard-FairVLMed dataset by LLM-generating QA pairs and then applying an LLM self-check quality filter; note the quote spans three source lines and contains two newlines. Race is restricted to White/Asian/Black and language to English/Spanish/Other. audits_selection = no and literal = no: only within-benchmark group distributions are shown (Figure 7), never compared to FairVLMed's parent population, the Mass Eye and Ear catchment, or census. Searched the file for missing/unknown/not reported/declined/imputation/complete case: no hits about their own data.

title: Equitable Length of Stay Prediction for Patients with Learning Disabilities and Multiple Long-term Conditions Using Machine Learning
notes: Ethnicity is the fairness attribute (FNR/FPR/balanced accuracy by ethnic group, Tables S14-S17); sex is handled by fitting and reporting entirely separate male and female models; age group and WIMD deprivation quintile have long-stay rates reported by group in Table S2, which is why age and ses are listed. Ethnicity 'Unknown' (~25% of patients) is retained and analysed as its own group, hence separate_category. audits_selection coded no: there is a CONSORT flow diagram and exclusion counts but no demographic breakdown of who was excluded, and no comparison of the cohort's ethnic composition to Welsh or SAIL population figures; grep for census/general population/represent found only outcome-level comparisons to prior literature (e.g. Black patients having longer LOS in a US study), not composition denominators.

title: FairDiffusion: Enhancing Equity in Latent Diffusion Models via Fair Bayesian Perturbation
notes: Authors constructed and curated the FairGenMed dataset (10,000 subjects who received glaucoma services 2015-2022 at one academic eye hospital, split 6,000/1,000/3,000), so cohort_is_filtered = yes per the benchmark-curation rule. audits_selection coded no: the paper notes 'size imbalances in the training dataset' and repeatedly calls Black/Hispanic 'historically underrepresented groups', but never compares retained group composition to a pre-selection or source denominator, and gives no retention rate by group. audits_selection_literal also no: the only representativeness statement ('it currently only features patients from the US') cites no external figure. protected_attributes: gender/race/ethnicity for FairGenMed; age and skin type additionally appear for the HAM10000 and CheXpert evaluations (Figures 7 and 8). Metrics are FID/IS/AUC-based equity-scaled variants (ES-FID, ES-IS, ES-AUC), maximum discrepancy, and DEOdds; ES-FID/ES-IS have no clean label in the metric vocabulary so 'other' is included. Missingness in race/gender/ethnicity is never mentioned and the reported category counts sum exactly to 10,000.

title: Evidence for Phenotype-Driven Disparities in Freezing of Gait Detection and Approaches to Bias Mitigation
notes: Wearable freezing-of-gait detection across four public PD datasets (Daphnet, De Souza, DeFOG, tDCS FOG; N=145). Strong model audit (DPR/EOR/EOD by sex, age, disease duration and FOG phenotype) plus four mitigation strategies. HARD CASE on audits_selection_literal: the discussion says the dataset phenotype imbalance 'reflected documented FOG phenotype distributions' citing literature, and the intro cites an external figure ('tremulous and akinetic manifestations co-occur in over 80% of patients'), but no numeric comparison is drawn between the datasets' composition and any external denominator, so I coded literal=no — the comparison is qualitative and concerns a clinical phenotype rather than demographic retention. protected_attributes restricted to the allowed vocabulary; the paper also disaggregates by FOG phenotype and disease duration, which have no label in the list. Filtering is dataset-level curation plus windowing; no patient-level inclusion/exclusion flow is reported anywhere.

title: Moving Beyond Medical Exams: A Clinician-Annotated Fairness Dataset of Real-World Tasks and Ambiguity in Mental Healthcare
notes: Author-constructed clinician-written vignette benchmark (MENTAT, 203 base questions). Filtering coded yes on the basis of author curation and the 90/10 evaluation/few-shot split; additional narrowing includes 'The most common mental health disorders were prioritized for this dataset' and a footnote restricting the age variable to 18-65 years. Patient demographics are assigned by design (each question resampled across gender/ethnicity/age), so there is no source population and no missing protected attribute; grep for census, representative, missing, imputation, complete case, exclude found no comparison of the item set's demographic composition to any external figure (Appendix D discusses U.S.-centricity qualitatively only). Only exclusion mentioned is dropping the Meditron-7b model from figures, which is a model exclusion, not a cohort filter.

title: Bias Evaluation and Mitigation in Retrieval-Augmented Medical Question-Answering Systems
notes: Benchmark/vignette study: demographic attributes are synthetically injected into MedQA/MedMCQA/MMLU/EquityMedQA question stems, so 'cohort' is an author-constructed evaluation set; coded cohort_is_filtered 'yes' per the rule that author sampling/curation of benchmark items counts, using the 'selectively incorporate demographic contexts' statement. There is no source population denominator anywhere, so both selection fields are 'no'. 'other' in fairness_metrics = retrieval overlap (IoU of retrieved documents across demographic variants).

title: Hybrid Adaptive Conformal Offline Reinforcement Learning for Fair Population Health Management
notes: HARD CASE for cohort_is_filtered rather than for audits_selection. The Waymark operational dataset (2.77M steps, 168,126 patients) is not described as narrowed by clinical inclusion criteria; the only described curation is the loader merging subgroup covariates 'prioritizing rows with more complete demographics', plus a 20k-row stratified subset for FQE and ~2000-episode stratified subsets for the IQL/CQL baselines. I coded yes because demographic-completeness-based row prioritization is dataset-level curation the authors themselves describe, but this is a weaker filter than the explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria in the other papers in this batch. audits_selection is 'no': the paper reports subgroup sample sizes and means within the final pool (Table 2) and bootstrap p-values against the largest-n subgroup, but never against a pre-selection or external denominator. Note the sex imputation (unknown folded into male) is an unaudited protected-attribute manipulation the authors flag only in passing.

title: Limitations of Public Chest Radiography Datasets for Artificial Intelligence: Label Quality, Domain Shift, Bias and Evaluation Challenges
notes: HARD CASE: borderline for audits_selection_literal, coded no. The paper filters each public dataset (PA view only, six harmonised labels, one-sided-selection undersampling, 80/10/10 patient-wise split) and then reports subgroup performance and the demographic composition of the resulting subsets (Table 4). It repeatedly links poor subgroup performance to under-representation ('reflecting their minority representation (19.1%, 31.8%, and 6.3%)'), and narratively states that public CXR datasets 'underrepresent paediatric, elderly, and minority populations' and that MIMIC-CXR label distributions 'diverge substantially from general hospital populations'. But those are citations to prior work with no specific external figure, and the composition of the retained subsets is never compared to the pre-filter datasets, a catchment, or census - so neither the strict nor the permissive criterion is met. null_attribute_handling coded drops because MIMIC-CXR is excluded entirely from the subgroup analysis for lack of age/sex metadata; this is dataset-level rather than record-level dropping.

title: Adapting Large Language Models to Mitigate Skin Tone Biases in Clinical Dermatology Tasks: A Mixed-Methods Study
notes: HARD CASE for the permissive reading. Strict audits_selection = no: the authors never report retention rates by skin tone or compare included vs excluded cases; their fairness work is entirely model-level (parity per Fitzpatrick type). For audits_selection_literal I went yes because Appendix 1 gives the specific parent-dataset skin tone distribution (SCIN: I 7.5% ... VI 5.7%, darker tones 'underrepresented') while the Methods state the study's own 300/600 selected cases were chosen for 'balanced representation across Fitzpatrick skin tones 1-6' - i.e. the retained sample's composition is set against a specific source-database figure. It is a borderline call: the juxtaposition is implicit rather than an explicit side-by-side comparison, and the paper never states its own cohort's numeric per-tone composition.

title: Fairness in Multi-modal Medical Diagnosis with Demonstration Selection
notes: HARD CASE: this paper does audit a selection step for differential representation across groups - the Max Diff metric (Table 4) quantifies the largest inter-group proportion gap among the DEMONSTRATIONS selected by each in-context-learning strategy (Random Race Max Diff 67.30%, Similarity 65.88%, FADS-Interactive 0.00%), and Figure 4 states that similarity selection 'overrepresents majority groups' and 'excludes the Black subgroup'. I coded audits_selection = no for two reasons: (a) the selected demonstrations are a modelling component, not the cohort on which the fairness metric is computed (the AD metrics are computed on the held-out test set), and (b) Max Diff is a within-set imbalance measure - max(ratio) minus min(ratio) among the selected exemplars - not a comparison against the labelled pool as a pre-selection denominator, which the rules explicitly place under 'reporting group sizes / class imbalance within the final cohort'. audits_selection_literal also no: no external or source figure is ever given, only parity as the referent. A coder taking the demonstration pool as the 'filter' could reasonably code this yes on the permissive reading. cohort_is_filtered = yes: authors curate balanced CheXpert Plus subsets and use the pre-split FairCLIP Glaucoma set (7K/2K/1K). null_attribute_handling = separate_category: ethnicity carries an explicit 'Unknown' level in the annotation scheme; the paper never otherwise discusses missing demographics (only one mention of 'missing demographic annotations', in Related Work about other studies).

title: Improving Fairness of Large Language Model-Based ICU Mortality Prediction via Case-Based Prompting
notes: LLM (Qwen3-32B) ICU mortality prediction on MIMIC-IV, n=45,153, with case-based prompting for mitigation. Clear model audit: subgroup AUROC, EOD (FNR difference) by sex, age and race, plus a feature-dependence similarity analysis (Jaccard/cosine/JS divergence) coded as 'other'. Table 2 compares the TRAIN vs TEST split demographics with p-values, not retained vs excluded patients, and no pre-selection denominator appears anywhere, so both selection fields are 'no'. null_attribute_handling coded unclear rather than 'imputes': patients with excessively high missing-data ratios were excluded and remaining missing values MICE-imputed, but this is a general statement about clinical variables and the paper never states what happened to records missing race or sex specifically (race categories are White/Black/Asian/Other with no Unknown group).

title: Multilevel Determinants of Overweight and Obesity Among U.S. Children Aged 10-17: Comparative Evaluation of Statistical and Machine Learning Approaches Using the 2021 National Survey of Children's Health
notes: NSCH 2021 survey, n=18,792 children aged 10-17. Filtering: age restriction to 10-17, complete-information requirement, and removal of underweight cases. null_attribute_handling is internally contradictory in the paper: Section 3.1 says the analytic sample requires 'complete information for the outcome variable and the selected predictors' (complete-case = drops) while Section 3.2.1 says 'We impute missing values in all predictors so that every model receives the same completed dataset' (imputes). Race and sex are among the predictors, so I coded imputes on the more specific and explicit handling statement, but a coder reading the complete-case sentence as authoritative would code drops. audits_selection_literal = no: the paper calls NSCH 'nationally representative' and cites CDC national obesity prevalence figures in the intro, but never compares the analytic sample's demographic composition to census or national figures; note Table 1 reports an implausible race distribution (Hispanic 76.7%, White non-Hispanic 7.5%) that goes uncommented, which itself suggests no representativeness check was done. The paper does state 'unequal subgroup representation' as a driver of disparities but supplies no external denominator.

title: Anterior's Approach to Fairness Evaluation of Automated Prior Authorization System
notes: HARD CASE: this is the closest paper in the batch to a selection audit. Appendix Table 3 reports each protected attribute's category counts (e.g., White 757 / Non-White 164 / Missing 6,226) as percentages of the FULL pre-filter reviewed-case set (N=7,166), and Section 4.1 reports the shrunken per-attribute analysis cohorts (Sex 6,505; Race 920; SES 1,929), so the retained analytic subsets ARE expressed against a pre-selection denominator - I coded audits_selection_literal 'yes' on that basis. I coded strict audits_selection 'no' because there is no comparison of retention/composition BETWEEN groups (race is unknown for the 86.9% dropped, so differential retention by race is not and cannot be tested here), no included-vs-excluded table, and no test of whether exclusion depended on a protected attribute. The paper does report complete-case robustness checks (Appendix A.3) and explicitly conditions its fairness claims on documented cases, which is selection-aware but not a selection audit under the strict definition.

title: FairLogue: A Toolkit for Intersectional Fairness Analysis in Clinical Machine Learning Models
notes: HARD CASE: this paper explicitly filters ON the protected attribute and never audits that filter. The toolkit optionally drops subgroups below a representation threshold, Table 1 footnotes state 'Demographic groups with n<20 held out', and minority upsampling is applied — yet no comparison is made between the retained 3,880-participant cohort and the All of Us parent database or any external population, so audits_selection and audits_selection_literal are both 'no'. The Introduction praises All of Us for 'recruiting traditionally underrepresented populations' but cites no figure for the cohort's composition versus All of Us or the US population, which under the rules does not count as a representativeness statement with a specific external figure. null_attribute_handling coded 'unclear': the only relevant sentence says the framework builds the intersectional identifier 'by imputing the protected characteristics', but the paper never discusses missing race/gender values, so I cannot tell whether this is missing-value imputation or simply concatenation of the two attributes. Cohort characteristics are deferred to supplemental Table S2, which is not in the provided full text.

title: FairEnc: A Fair Vision-Language Model with Fair Vision and Text Encoders for Glaucoma Detection
notes: Method paper with a full model audit: group-wise AUC, worst-group AUC, ES-AUC, DPD and DEOdds per attribute on Harvard-FairVLMed (race, gender, ethnicity, language) and on the authors' new FairFundus set (gender, age). fairness_metrics includes 'other' for ES-AUC and worst-group AUC. cohort_is_filtered = yes under the benchmark-construction clause: FairFundus was collected and curated by the authors (single Egyptian site, 1,158 image-note pairs from 656 patients, optic-disc crops converted to grayscale), and race/ethnicity/language were dropped as evaluation attributes there for lack of variability. audits_selection = no: the paper notes that Harvard-FairVLMed race and language distributions are 'highly imbalanced' (Figure 1) and that FairFundus has limited demographic variability, but gives no pre-selection or external denominator figure, so the permissive reading is also no. Searched for missing/imputation/complete case/unknown: the only 'unknown attribute' text is in Related Work about other methods, not the authors' own data handling.

title: Worst-Group Equalized Odds Regularization for Multi-Attribute Fair Medical Image Classification
notes: EOdds/EOM are reported separately for Age, Race and Sex in Table 2, so the model is audited on the pool. Filtering is explicit for MIMIC-CXR (only patients with Pleural Effusion, Cardiomegaly or Atelectasis, 82,282 images) and the RNFL-OCT cohort is described as 'racially balanced', i.e. curated. Table 1 gives only final subgroup sample sizes with no pre-filter denominator, and greps for exclud/missing/unknown/census/underrepresent returned nothing, so both selection fields are no and null handling is not_mentioned.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Machine Learning for Type 2 Diabetes Risk Prediction: Large-Scale External Validation and Fairness Analysis
notes: HARD CASE on audits_selection_literal, coded YES. XGBoost type-2 diabetes risk model developed on NHANES 2015-2020 (n=15,685, complete-case, adults) and externally validated on BRFSS 2020-2022 (n=1,285,783). Table I explicitly compares the development cohort's composition (age, sex, smoking, BMI, physical activity, diabetes prevalence) against BRFSS with p-values as a 'distribution shift' analysis; under the permissive rule ('ANY comparison of the retained cohort's group composition to ANY external or source figure') that qualifies, since BRFSS is a large external national surveillance population. It is a development-vs-deployment shift check, NOT a differential-retention audit against the NHANES pre-selection denominator, so strict audits_selection=no. Second judgement call: null_attribute_handling coded reports_only from the Limitations statement that BRFSS race/ethnicity had 44.2% missingness which 'preclude[d] full equity analysis for this important demographic dimension' (race is consequently absent from the fairness table); the Preprocessing section separately says 'Median and mode were used to impute missing values in continuous and categorical variables, respectively', so 'imputes' is arguable. Fairness stratifiers actually reported are gender, age group and BMI category (BMI is clinical and not in the vocabulary). Two-column source text merged per line, so quotes are single-line substrings including hyphenated line breaks.

title: Can Zero-Shot LLMs Predict Child Malnutrition? A Fairness and Temporal Robustness Study
notes: Zero-shot GPT-4o-mini on BDHS 2007-2022, n=17,106. Clear complete-case filtering (age <5, complete anthropometry, no missing values on any selected feature); the stratifying attributes (child sex, residence, wealth index) are all selected features, so complete-case exclusion drops records missing them - coded drops. audits_selection = no: Table 1 stratifies the retained cohort by stunting outcome, not by retention, and there is no pre-filter denominator or per-group retention rate anywhere. audits_selection_literal = no: BDHS is described as 'nationally representative' but no external/census figure is compared to the cohort's composition. The re-run on the 3,568 poorest-category samples with the wealth feature removed is a model/feature ablation, not a selection audit.

title: Assessing and Mitigating Bias in Medical Artificial Intelligence: The Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Deep Learning Model for ECG Analysis.
notes: HARD CASE: audits_selection coded yes on a structural reading. Patients with missing/multiple race were dropped from analysis, and Table 1 reports that excluded 'Unknown' group (N=6,587) side by side with the five retained race groups, giving %male, age and comorbidity for included vs excluded patients (52,870 = 46,283 retained + 6,587 unknown). Coding rules list 'a table comparing demographics of included vs excluded patients' as qualifying, so I coded yes; however the authors never frame it as a selection audit, never test differential retention by race (impossible, since the excluded group is precisely the race-unknown group), and never state retention rates. A stricter coder could defensibly code this 'no'. Model performance itself is disaggregated only by race/ethnicity; the text notes prior work found consistency across age and sex but no age/sex metrics are reported here.

title: Why Inclusion Matters for Alzheimer's Disease Biomarker Discovery in Plasma.
notes: Race-stratified SVM performance (Table 3) is a clear model audit on the analysis pool. Cohort was filtered (only ADRC participants with banked plasma meeting criteria; non-Hispanic White participants demographically matched to the 56 available African American/Black participants), but no comparison of retained vs excluded/source composition is reported. The Introduction cites external participation figures (<~5% in trials, <~13% in AD research assessments) as background about the field, not as a denominator for this cohort's composition, so audits_selection_literal coded no. Missingness in the stratifying attribute (self-reported race) is never mentioned; the only missingness discussed is missing TMT protein values.

title: Obstetric comorbidity scores and disparities in severe maternal morbidity across marginalized groups.
venue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
notes: Population-based California birth cohort (n=3,308,554) with linked birth certificate/discharge data. Model audit is clear: C-statistic, PR-AUC, calibration and SMM rates reported separately by race-ethnicity, nativity, payment method and education. Cohort counts as filtered: 98.2% birth-certificate/discharge linkage rate plus per-analysis exclusion of subjects missing the stratifying sociodemographic factor (sample sizes in Tables 3/5 differ across strata for exactly this reason). No comparison of retained vs excluded/unlinked subjects by group, and no external/census denominator, so both selection fields are 'no'. Note 'nativity' (US-born vs foreign-born) is not in the prescribed label list but is genuinely disaggregated, so it is retained as a label.

title: Detecting Racial/Ethnic Health Disparities Using Deep Learning From Frontal Chest Radiography.
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
notes: Model AUROC is reported per cohort, not per demographic group; the by-group quantity is Δvasc (model-vs-administrative-code discrepancy) regressed on age, sex, race/ethnicity, language and SDI, plus logistic ORs for having any HCC code by race/ethnicity and language. Coded audits_model_on_pool=yes on the strength of these by-group error/outcome estimates. The paper compares its two cohorts (ambulatory vs hospitalized) to each other, but never compares the retained cohort to a pre-selection or external denominator, so both selection fields are 'no'. SDI is a zip-code-level deprivation index coded here as 'ses'.

title: Interpretability and fairness evaluation of deep learning models on MIMIC-IV dataset.
notes: Model audit is thorough (AUC per protected group, plus treatment-adoption rates by group = outcome_rate_by_group). Cohort filtering is explicit (45,768 -> 43,005) but only TOTAL counts are given at each filtering step; no demographic breakdown of who was dropped and no comparison to the full MIMIC-IV/BIDMC population. Records with 'None'/'Unknown'/'Unable to obtain' ethnicity are dropped from the fairness analysis, and Table 9 in the appendix shows UNKNOWN was 9.88% of admissions, but the paper never audits whether that missingness is differential. Coded audits_selection=no and audits_selection_literal=no.

title: Comparison between machine learning methods for mortality prediction for sepsis patients with different social determinants.
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
notes: Clear selection audit of the sepsis-identification filter: forest plots report, for each social-determinant subgroup, the PROPORTION of that subgroup in the 11,791-patient source cohort that each of six sepsis criteria retains, with bootstrap CIs, and significant between-subgroup differences in those retention proportions are reported. That is retention rate by group against a pre-filter denominator. Note the authors do NOT audit their own upstream exclusions (nonadults, missing data, cardiothoracic surgery); they explicitly defer this: they performed complete-case analysis and say they plan future work on 'the potential links between missing data and social determinants of health'. null_attribute_handling coded separate_category because unspecified race is folded into 'other' and unspecified marital status is kept as 'unknown'; this coexists with complete-case deletion of records missing data generally.

title: Fairness in the prediction of acute postoperative pain using machine learning models.
notes: Cohort narrowed 37,493 -> 14,263 via a selection flow (Figure 2) with no demographic breakdown of who was dropped, so audits_selection = no. BORDERLINE for audits_selection_literal: the Discussion asserts the cohort 'is reflective of the population of orthopedic surgery patients in the state of Florida' but cites no external figure, which the rules explicitly say does not count; coded no. null_attribute_handling coded unclear: imputation of 'missing variables' is stated generally for model predictors, but the paper never says what was done with records missing the stratifying attributes themselves (race/insurance/language have no Unknown category in Table 3).

title: Bias in machine learning models can be significantly mitigated by careful training: Evidence from neuroimaging studies.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
notes: Very short PNAS brief; cohort description is thin (three consortia: iSTAGING, PHENOM, ABIDE) with almost no inclusion/exclusion detail. cohort_is_filtered coded 'yes' on the strength of the explicit statement that the baseline network is trained on data 'after dropping missing values'; this is the only concrete narrowing the paper describes, so the coding is defensible but weakly supported. The paper reports the 87%/13% male/female imbalance in ASD, but that is class imbalance inside the final pool, not retention against a denominator, so audits_selection = no. The Discussion notes that women, minority ethnicity groups and older subjects are less likely to enrol in trials, but gives no figure for its own cohorts, so audits_selection_literal = no. null_attribute_handling coded separate_category from the general categorical-feature rule; the paper never states specifically what happens when the stratifying attribute itself is missing.

title: Racial and Ethnic Bias in Risk Prediction Models for Colorectal Cancer Recurrence When Race and Ethnicity Are Omitted as Predictors.
notes: HARD CASE: the paper states 'The membership of KPSC is socioeconomically diverse and reflects that of the Southern California census population' — an explicit representativeness claim referencing census. I coded audits_selection_literal='no' because (a) no specific external figure is given (only a citation) and (b) the claim is about the health-system membership, i.e. the source population, not about the retained analytic cohort relative to any denominator. A reviewer applying the permissive reading very loosely could flip this to yes. Strict audits_selection is clearly no. The multiracial/other group was dropped for small sample size (a filtering step, not a retention audit); 'no unknown or missing race and ethnicity' is coded reports_only since missingness is addressed (as zero) but no handling procedure is stated. Range difference between best- and worst-performing group is the disparity metric ('other').

title: Fairness of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Foregone Preventive Dental Care for Adults.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection_literal. Strict reading is clearly 'no': Table 1 describes the final cohort only, and there is no included-vs-excluded demographic comparison. For the PERMISSIVE reading I coded 'yes' on a judgement call: the authors explicitly compare their unweighted analytic sample against the MEPS survey-WEIGHTED (nationally representative) version of the same sample and report them as similar (eFigure 1/eFigure 2), which is a comparison of the retained cohort's composition against a population-representative referent. A reasonable coder could call this 'no' since the actual figures live in the supplement and no specific group percentages are compared in text. Note also 'The survey is designed to be representative of the US civilian noninstitutionalized population' is a representativeness claim with no specific figure attached, which by the rules does NOT count on its own. null_attribute_handling coded 'unclear': median imputation is stated for predictors generally, and race/age/income are predictors, but the paper never states what happened to records missing race/ethnicity, age, or income specifically; searched: missing, unknown, not reported, declined, imputation, complete case.

title: Evaluating Algorithmic Bias in 30-Day Hospital Readmission Models: Retrospective Analysis.
notes: Extensive MODEL audit (FNR/FPR/0-1 loss differences, GEI, AUC and Brier by race and income, stratified by hospital and by hospital racial composition) but no SELECTION audit: the cohort filter (age <18, in-hospital death, discharge against medical advice, insufficient readmission information) is reported only as a flow diagram (Figure 1) with no demographic breakdown of excluded admissions and no retention rate by group. Table 1 describes only the final cohort. Only external figure cited is that the SIDs capture >97% of eligible discharges, which is not group-specific, so audits_selection_literal is also no. The single occurrence of 'missing' in the paper refers to missing VisitLink/length of stay (outcome ascertainment), not to missing race or income; race missingness is never mentioned, hence not_mentioned. fairness_metrics list includes auroc_by_group and calibration_by_group from Table 3 (AUC and Brier by subgroup), which the quoted sentence does not name; 'other' = generalized entropy index.

title: Fairness in Predicting Cancer Mortality Across Racial Subgroups.
notes: Strong model audit (AUROC/F1 plus 3 fairness metrics across race). Table 1 compares alive vs deceased patients, i.e. by outcome, not included vs excluded, so it is not a selection audit. Native American patients (n=45) were dropped from subgroup analysis for small sample size, but no retention rate or pre-selection denominator is reported anywhere. 'Other or unknown' race and 'unknown'/'missing' ethnicity are retained and analysed as their own category, hence separate_category; note that other missing feature values were median-imputed.

title: Investigation of bias in the automated assessment of school violence.
notes: HARD CASE: this paper explicitly audits its own study design for bias using the PROBAST framework, including the participant-selection domain ('Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?') and acknowledges referral bias. That is a qualitative appraisal of the selection step, not a quantitative comparison of retained vs excluded group composition against a pre-selection denominator, and no demographic breakdown of the 412-401-387 attrition is given, so audits_selection = no under the strict rule. Coded literal = no as well: the representativeness statement is vague and cites no external figure. Health/clinical inclusion is satisfied (recruitment at Cincinnati Children's inpatient/outpatient units, forensic-psychiatrist reference standard). null_attribute_handling is mixed - Table 1 keeps 'Other or unknown' race/ethnicity and an 'unknown' education bin, but the bias analysis itself dropped the 14 students without complete demographics; coded 'drops' for the analysis that produced the disaggregated metric.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models.
notes: Exclusions (glaucoma-suspect-only codes; <4 months lookback) are stated without any demographic breakdown of who was excluded, so strict audits_selection is no. The paper does compare demographic composition ACROSS its own train/internal-test/external-site splits (e.g. White 65.6% vs 16.1% vs 46.0%), but those are alternative evaluation cohorts, not a pre-selection or external population denominator, so audits_selection_literal is also no. Race 'Unknown' (1.3%) and ethnicity 'Unknown' (3.5%) appear as rows in Table 3 but the paper never says how Unknown patients were assigned in the binary White/non-White and Hispanic/non-Hispanic contrasts, hence reports_only rather than separate_category.

title: Predicting Prenatal Depression and Assessing Model Bias Using Machine Learning Models.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection_literal. The cohort drops from 5875 extracted to 2414 analysed, and only total counts are given for that drop - no by-group retention rates, so strict audits_selection = no. For the permissive reading I coded 'yes': the paper states a specific external referent, the hospital catchment composition (52% NHB, 29% H, 9% NHW, 10% Asian/Native American), and separately reports the analysed sample as 54% NHB and 27% (Results section says '27% NHW' but from Table 1 / abstract this is Latina, an apparent typo in the paper). The side-by-side comparison is left implicit - the paper never writes a sentence comparing the two - so a stricter coder could call this 'no'. null_attribute_handling: MICE imputation is stated for missing data generally; the paper never says what was done with records missing race/ethnicity, hence 'unclear'. Searched: missing, unknown, not reported, declined, imputation, complete case.

title: Evaluating Bias-Mitigated Predictive Models of Perinatal Mood and Anxiety Disorders.
notes: Model audit only (demographic parity and false-negative-rate differences vs non-Hispanic White patients, AUROC per race/ethnicity per fold). Cohort is filtered (only birthing individuals admitted to the postpartum/maternal-fetal care unit, live births only, no prenatal or stillbirth records, first complete record per patient; 19,790 records reduced to 19,430 patients) but the drop from full to final dataset is never broken down by race/ethnicity, so no selection audit. The introduction cites external literature that racial and ethnic minority women are less likely to be screened at all, i.e. the authors are aware their cohort is a screened subpopulation, but they never quantify their cohort against any pre-selection or census denominator, so audits_selection_literal is no. Missing race handled as separate 'unknown' category and explicitly retained.

title: Survival After Radical Cystectomy for Bladder Cancer: Development of a Fair Machine Learning Model.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection_literal. 374,881 patients were screened down to 16,481 with no demographic breakdown of exclusions, so the strict code is no. The Discussion, however, cites specific external epidemiologic figures (bladder cancer ~4x more common in males; ~2x more common in White populations) and states this skew 'was reflected in our study', which is an explicit representativeness statement anchored to a specific external figure; I coded audits_selection_literal = yes on that basis, while noting it references disease incidence rather than a source-population denominator, so a stricter reader could code it no. American Indian/Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander patients were excluded a priori as separate groups for small sample size, but this is an exclusion decision, not an audit of it, and no handling of records with missing race/sex is described.

title: Mitigating bias in AI mortality predictions for minority populations: a transfer learning approach.
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
notes: CDC COVID-19 Case Surveillance Restricted Access data, heavily filtered (laboratory-confirmed only, death outcome only, invalid/Unknown/Missing race-ethnicity dropped) down to 365,608 cases. Per-race performance tables (Tables 2-4) plus equalized-odds TPR/FPR make audits_model_on_pool clearly yes. The paper reports the post-filter group counts (252,125 NH White, 43,304 NH Black, 19,385 Hispanic, 5,667 Asian, 651 American Indian) but never states the pre-filter group counts or a retention rate by group, so this is group sizes within the final cohort, which the rules explicitly say does NOT qualify. Discussion repeatedly attributes bias to 'underrepresentation of minority populations in the training datasets' but cites no external denominator, so literal = no as well.

title: Bias in Prediction Models to Identify Patients With Colorectal Cancer at High Risk for Readmission After Resection.
notes: Classic CONSORT-style exclusion accounting: total counts excluded (missing readmission data, in-hospital death, LOS>20 days) with no demographic breakdown and no retention rate by race, so audits_selection is no. The only external-comparison statement is that NSQIP underrepresents smaller/community hospitals — about hospitals, not patient group composition, and with no figure — so audits_selection_literal is no as well. Patients with unrecorded race (18%) are retained as an explicit 'Unknown/Not Reported' group and carried through modelling and Table 2, hence separate_category. Model performance is disaggregated only by race; Table 2 additionally reports readmission ORs by sex, age group and Hispanic ethnicity, but those are covariate ORs rather than group-stratified model metrics, so protected_attributes is limited to race.

title: Leveraging Machine Learning to Predict and Assess Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity in Maryland.
notes: The disaggregation here is of the OUTCOME (unadjusted relative risk of SMM by race-ethnicity, income, insurance, language), not of model performance - the ML performance metrics (AUC, precision, recall) are reported overall only, never by group. Coded audits_model_on_pool=yes on the rules' explicit allowance for 'outcome rate by ethnicity'. Cohort is near-census (the SID is the universe of Maryland inpatient discharges) but is still narrowed to delivery hospitalizations and to ages 12-55 by the CDC SMM algorithm. No pre-selection denominator comparison of any kind; the only external comparison is a national SMM PREVALENCE figure (146.8 to 179.8 per 10,000), which is an outcome rate, not cohort composition, so it does not count for audits_selection_literal. Missingness in race/income/insurance/language is never mentioned anywhere in the text.

title: Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms Identifying Children at Increased Risk of Out-of-Home Placement: Development and Practical Considerations.
notes: Model audit only: partial AUROC at specificity >=90% compared between Black and White children for each of four models. Cohort filtered to Medicaid-enrolled children <18 in two Ohio InCK counties. Cohort race composition (69% White, 9% Black, 18% unknown/missing) is reported with no denominator; national foster-care disproportionality figures appear in the Introduction (Black children 21% of foster care entries vs 14% of US child population) but are about the child welfare system generally, not a comparison of this cohort against a source population, so both selection fields are no. null_attribute_handling coded drops because children with unknown/missing race (18% of the sample) were excluded from the racial bias analysis (jointly with Asian and Native American children, for small-N reasons) although they were retained in model training and appear as an 'Other or unknown' row in Table 1; separate_category is a defensible alternative. Table 1 also reports placement rates by gender, but the disaggregated model performance metric is race only.

title: Evaluating fairness of machine learning prediction of prolonged wait times in Emergency Department with Interpretable eXtreme gradient boosting.
notes: Clear model audit (FNR/AUROC and formal group fairness metrics by sex, race/ethnicity, insurance) plus counterfactual fairness. This is the clearest example in the batch of a filter that could plausibly bias the fairness estimate and is never audited: visits missing race/ethnicity, sex, marital status or language are dropped outright, and no count, rate, or demographic comparison of dropped vs retained visits is given. Language/marital status appear in Table 1 but performance is not disaggregated by them, so they are not listed as protected_attributes.

title: External validation of a proprietary risk model for 1-year mortality in community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older.
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
notes: External validation of the Epic End-of-Life Care Index in 215,731 community-dwelling adults 65+. Strong model audit: Table 2 gives sensitivity/PPV/specificity/NPV by sex, race, ethnicity and age, and Table 3 gives equal-opportunity differences and ratios per attribute. Cohort is filtered by age 65+, health-system membership and a July 2023 index date. No comparison of the retained cohort against the health system's 24-county catchment population or any census figure; the only representativeness language is the unquantified limitation that 'certain populations were not well-represented', which the rules say does not count. null_attribute_handling coded separate_category because patients who declined to report race/ethnicity are retained and folded into the 'Other' and 'Not Hispanic or Latino' analysis categories rather than dropped; note this is folding-into-an-existing-category rather than a distinct 'Unknown' stratum.

title: Implicit bias in ICU electronic health record data: measurement frequencies and missing data rates of clinical variables.
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
notes: HARD CASE: this paper audits differential DATA AVAILABILITY (missing-data rates and measurement frequencies for clinical variables) by race, gender and age — conceptually adjacent to a selection audit — but the object audited is missingness of vitals/labs WITHIN the retained cohort, not differential retention produced by the cohort filter. The filter itself (age >=18, no pregnancy, >24h stay, arterial line present; 25,606 patients dropped for lacking an arterial line alone) is never examined for demographic differential retention, and the retained cohort is never compared to the full MIMIC-III population. I therefore coded audits_selection=no and audits_selection_literal=no; the limitation sentence about MIMIC-III being 'predominantly older and White' has no external figure. Ethnicity 'Missing' (14.7%) is a row in Table 1 but the paper does not state whether that group entered the TMLE contrasts, so reports_only. Insurance, language, marital status and religion were also examined (Appendix D) but are not in the quoted list. The 'metric' compared across groups is an adjusted mean count, not a standard fairness metric.

title: Bias in vital signs? Machine learning models can learn patients' race or ethnicity from the values of vital signs alone.
notes: HARD CASE, two ways. (1) Inclusion: the AUCs are for a race/ethnicity-PREDICTION task, i.e. AUC indexed by pairs of racial groups, not model performance disaggregated within groups; the paper also reports vital-sign values and p-values separately by ethnic group (Table 1). I included it and coded audits_model_on_pool=yes because performance is reported broken out by racial group pairing, but this is not a conventional model fairness audit. fairness_metrics coded 'other' rather than auroc_by_group for that reason. (2) audits_selection: the filter from 200,859 eICU admissions to 10,763 is severe and requires recorded race, yet no pre-filter racial composition of eICU-CRD is given. The paper does report the counts of racial groups it then discarded (Asian American 177, Native American 84) and notes 'only 10% of the patients in the original dataset are Black', but 'original dataset' refers to the already-extracted 10,763, not the parent database. I coded both strict and literal 'no' because there is no comparison of the retained cohort's composition against a pre-selection or external denominator - only within-post-filter group sizes.

title: Ensemble learning to enhance accurate identification of patients with glaucoma using electronic health records.
notes: Model audit only (equalized odds difference by sex, race, ethnicity at both sites, plus the authors' Target Probability Difference metric = 'other'). Cohort filtered: SOURCE EHR data restricted to patients aged 40-80 with at least 2 eye-care visits, then 1728 randomly selected patients (900 UoM, 828 SU) chart-reviewed by ophthalmologists. The paper reports the racial/sex composition of each site's glaucoma patients and notes the external cohort 'may not fully represent' the internal site's population, but this is cohort-vs-cohort, not cohort against a pre-selection or source denominator and no retention rate by group is given, so both selection fields are no (borderline for the permissive field; I went no because no source-population figure is cited). null_attribute_handling is unclear: the only mention of missingness is a speculative discussion sentence attributing possible undetected bias to 'missing data or less representation of certain subgroups', with no statement of how records missing sex/race/ethnicity were treated.

title: Performance of 4 Methods to Assess Health-Related Social Needs.
notes: BORDERLINE for audits_selection_literal: the Results state 'The sample was reflective of an urban, adult primary care population (Table 1)' but cite no external or catchment figure, which the rules say does not qualify; coded no. Recruitment was a convenience series (author-constructed sample), counted as filtering per the benchmark/sampling rule. Race/ethnicity is self-reported with an 'Other, multiple, or unknown' category retained in Table 1 and folded into the 'all others' fairness stratum, hence separate_category; the only other missingness statement ('Missing values (eg, no diagnoses or prior encounters) were classified as zero') concerns EHR predictors, not the protected attribute.

title: Racial and socioeconomic disparities in long term survival after surgery and radiation for spinal cord hemangioblastoma.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection: the paper does run a Mann-Kendall trend test on the racial composition of the cohort over 2004-2017. That is a within-cohort temporal stability check, not a comparison against a pre-selection or source denominator, so it is coded 'no'; flagged because it is the closest thing to a composition audit in the batch that still fails the rule. The NCDB parent database size (~34 million cases) is stated, and SEER incidence (0.014 per 100,000) is cited in the Introduction, but neither is used to compare the cohort's demographic composition, so literal = no. Disaggregated metrics are outcome rates (30-day/90-day/5-year/10-year/long-term mortality, LOS, readmission) and KM survival by race, insurance and facility type, plus an ML survival model whose SHAP importances include race - so audits_model_on_pool = yes on the outcome-rate criterion. Race categories are only White/Black/Asian and sum exactly to N=716; the paper never mentions missing/unknown race or how other race groups were handled, hence not_mentioned (the only 'missing data' mention is a generic retrospective-design limitation).

title: Quantifying device type and handedness biases in a remote Parkinson's disease AI-powered assessment.
notes: Authors constructed the dataset themselves by convenience recruitment (primarily adults 50+, recruited through Parkinson's advocacy organizations and two symposiums) and then curated it (Linux users dropped, race upsampling, SMOTE), so cohort_is_filtered=yes. The paper repeatedly flags underrepresentation of non-White and female participants, but always relative to its own sample composition — never against a census, catchment, or pre-recruitment denominator — so both selection fields are no. Confirmed by grep that the strings missing/unknown/not reported/declined/imputation/complete case appear nowhere in the file, hence not_mentioned for null handling. Device type is coded as 'ses' because the authors explicitly frame it as 'a proxy for socioeconomic factors'; dominant hand has no label in the coding vocabulary and is not listed.

title: Deep Learning with Disc Photos or OCT Scans in Glaucoma Detection.
notes: Borderline for audits_selection: the paper DOES run chi-square tests on race, sex and ethnicity - but between the TRAINING and TESTING splits, both of which are post-selection. That is a randomisation check, not a comparison against a pre-selection or external denominator, so I coded 'no' for both strict and literal. Several substantial filters (reliable VF within 30 days of OCT, OCT quality score >=6, unclear glaucomatous status omitted, one eye per patient) are applied with no per-group retention reported. null_attribute_handling coded 'drops' because the ethnicity-stratified AUCs explicitly exclude the 773 patients lacking ethnicity data; note that Table 1 separately retains N/A as a descriptive category (race N/A 13.7%, ethnicity N/A 4.6%), so 'separate_category' applies to the descriptive table but not to the fairness analysis. Terms 'missing'/'unknown' do not appear; the paper uses 'N/A' and 'chose not to disclose'.

title: Detecting, Characterizing, and Mitigating Implicit and Explicit Racial Biases in Health Care Datasets With Subgroup Learnability: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection, coded no. The paper is entirely about dataset composition (AEquity guides how many samples to collect from each racial group), and it does state that for 4 of 9 findings AEquity 'resulted in the curation of a dataset reflecting the underlying empirical group frequencies' - a loose comparison of the curated dataset to the parent dataset's group frequencies. But no numeric group composition, retention rate or pre-selection denominator is reported, and the sampling being described is the authors' deliberate intervention rather than an audited filter, so neither the strict nor the permissive criterion is met. Cohorts are author-constructed samples (n=1024 race-balanced subsets, curation up to 30,000 samples, NHANES preprocessed to N=47,261), which counts as filtering. Missingness in race/sex/insurance is never mentioned anywhere in the text (verified by search). Protected attributes: race and Medicaid/socioeconomic status per the quote; sex also audited ('AEquity remains valid for mitigation of performance bias by sex').

title: Developing and Validating Machine Learning-Driven Risk Indices to Predict Patient Dropout During Referral, Evaluation, and Waitlisting for Kidney Transplant.
notes: This paper DOES audit its own selection step, which is the rarer finding: it prespecified a sensitivity analysis comparing included vs excluded referral patients on age and sex (both non-significant) and explicitly flags in the Limitations that '~14% of referred patients were excluded due to loss to follow-up or death, introducing potential selection bias'. Coded audits_selection = yes, though the comparison covers only age and sex (race/ethnicity, the paper's main equity axis, was not compared) because the authors state referral-level data for excluded patients were limited. audits_model_on_pool is coded yes on the basis of the racial composition of model-assigned risk strata and race-stratified outcome/characteristic rates; note that AUROC itself is reported overall (0.71-0.79) and never separately by race, and no formal fairness metric is computed.

title: A fairness-aware machine learning framework for maternal health in Ghana: integrating explainability, bias mitigation, and causal inference for ethical AI deployment.
notes: HARD CASE: the Methods section 'Handling of missing data' states that completely missing data on key ANC variables were 'Assessed for patterns of missingness to evaluate potential bias' - an explicit intention to check whether the filter is differential - but no such analysis, breakdown or result is ever reported, and the missingness concerned is in the outcome/ANC variables rather than the protected attributes. Coded 'no' for both selection fields on that basis. Also considered for the permissive reading: DHS sampling weights are applied 'to ensure nationally representative estimates' and the Introduction cites the 2022 Ghana Maternal Health Survey figure (35% with 8+ ANC contacts), but neither is a comparison of the retained cohort's group composition to an external figure, so literal stays 'no'. Analysis sample of 3,314 women is derived by explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (live birth or stillbirth within 24 months, complete pregnancy-outcome timing). Protected attributes listed are the four used in the AIF360 audit; Table 1 and the AOR model additionally disaggregate by age, education, residence and health insurance.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Risk Stratification in Chronic Kidney Disease Progression: Minimizing Bias via Race-Specific Algorithms.
notes: HARD CASE, and a borderline INCLUDE. The paper is self-described as a PRISMA systematic review, but its analytic cohort is largely SYNTHETIC: 'we created synthetic patient-level samples based on the published population characteristics of the NHANES, CRIC, and UK Biobank studies' and 'We simulated realistic performance data, including fairness diagnostics'; some reported numbers are labelled '(hypothetical illustration)'. I included it because it does report by-race model metrics on a defined (if simulated) patient-level cohort, but every field should be read as applying to a simulated cohort. On selection: Table 1 lists the racial composition of the three parent datasets (e.g. UK Biobank 94% White) and the Results state the analytic cohort was 'by design' 60% White / 40% Black, but the paper never draws a comparison between the two, never reports retention by group, and the composition is a design choice rather than a filtering outcome — so I coded both audits_selection and audits_selection_literal 'no'. A permissive coder could argue literal=yes from Table 1 plus the by-design composition; I went no because no comparison is actually made. Null handling coded unclear: the only statement about missing race is a forward-looking deployment concern; the preprocessing text says missing categorical data was 'handled either as its own category when this made sense clinically or ... coded as absent' but never says this applied to the race stratifier.

title: Machine learning performance for a small dataset: random oversampling improves data imbalances and fairness.
notes: Borderline-but-clear 'no' for audits_selection. The paper is unusually explicit that a filter removed a group (Medicare + VA, N = 280, i.e. 58.2% of the sample, censored out of the socioeconomic analysis) and that socioeconomic subgroups are 'underrepresented'. But Table 2 gives only within-cohort subgroup sizes ('Sub-Population Census' is the authors' term for their own group counts, not an external census), and there is no retention rate by group and no comparison against a pre-selection denominator. Robeson County external figures are cited (33.1% poverty rate, county health rankings) but as context for the setting, never compared to the cohort's own SES composition, so audits_selection_literal is also 'no'. Missingness of race/marital status/insurance is never mentioned anywhere in the paper. Note the Results/Discussion partly contradict the Abstract on whether equalized odds disparity fell with oversampling.

title: Classifying Delayed Dental Care Using Machine Learning: A National Health Interview Survey Analysis.
notes: Disaggregation is of the OUTCOME (prevalence of delayed dental care by age, sex, education, insurance, race in Table 1), not of model performance: the ML models are evaluated only in aggregate (accuracy/precision/recall/F1 on the held-out test set), so audits_model_on_pool is yes only under the rule's 'performance OR outcome metric' wording. Cohort is filtered by explicit exclusion criteria that delete records with Refused/Don't know or missing key predictors including sex, education, income and insurance, i.e. protected-attribute missingness is handled by dropping. No comparison of the retained sample to the full NHIS Sample Adult file or to census figures is made; survey weights are applied to obtain nationally representative estimates but weighting is not a comparison against an external figure, so audits_selection_literal is no (borderline). Note an internal inconsistency in the paper: N=54,927 is given both as the Sample Adult file size and as the post-exclusion analytic sample.

title: Equity and Transportability of Plasma ATN Phenotypes in a Population-Representative U.S. Aging Cohort.
venue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
notes: HARD CASE. The paper's whole transportability framing compares its analytic sample against a population denominator: survey weights post-stratified to Current Population Survey totals, with weighted vs unweighted composition contrasted directly (78.9% vs 65.2% White etc.) and 'Differences between weighted and unweighted estimates quantify selection bias'. Under the permissive reading that is a comparison of cohort composition to national statistics, so audits_selection_literal = yes. Under the strict reading it is NOT differential retention against a pre-selection denominator: the weighted/unweighted gap reflects the HRS oversampling design rather than any retention rate, and the authors' own filter (9,934 venous blood participants -> 4,427 analysed, with only n=38 attributed to missing biomarker data) is never broken down by group; healthy-volunteer selection is acknowledged in the Limitations but not quantified by group. Coded strict no. Missingness in race/ethnicity, sex or education is never mentioned; the only missingness discussed is biomarker missingness (<1%, IPW sensitivity analysis).

title: Fairness analysis of machine learning predictions of aggression in acute psychiatric care.
notes: Most thorough model audit in the batch: FPR/TPR/F1/ROC/calibration by race-ethnicity, gender, admission mode, citizenship and housing, plus an intersectional race x gender analysis. Cohort filtered to ED-route inpatient admissions with corrections/hospital transfers excluded, capped at three prediction windows per visit. No selection audit: nothing compares the retained cohort's composition to CAMH's wider inpatient population, Toronto demographics, or the excluded transfers; Table 1 compares incident vs no-incident days, which is an outcome comparison, not a retention comparison. null_attribute_handling is two-stage - variables with <=20% missing imputed by mode, variables with >20% missing (citizenship, housing, marital status, admission mode) given an explicit 'missing' category, and then all individuals with imputed values for a given attribute are excluded from that attribute's fairness analysis. Coded 'drops' because that exclusion governs the cohort on which the disaggregated metrics are actually computed; note race/ethnicity was 17% missing and mode-imputed before those records were dropped from the race fairness analysis. 'admission mode' is disaggregated too but has no label in the prescribed list.

title: Leveraging Explainable AI to Identify Determinants of Lifetime HIV Testing Among Adults in Tennessee, United States: Evidence for Targeted Public Health Strategies From BRFSS 2023.
venue: Journal of primary care & community health
notes: HARD CASE (borderline on both inclusion and audits_selection_literal). Included under criterion (ii) because the OUTCOME (lifetime HIV testing) is reported disaggregated by race, sex, age, income, education, marital status, insurance, urbanicity and disability burden (Table 2, weighted % and CORs/AORs). NOTE: the ML models' performance (AUROC, PR-AUC, F1) is reported only overall — there is no by-group model performance metric at all, so audits_model_on_pool rests entirely on the disaggregated outcome rates. On selection: the cohort was narrowed to Tennessee respondents with a non-missing HIV-testing outcome, and the paper never reports how many were dropped or whether dropping varied by group. It does compare its weighted prevalence estimate (38.8%) to an external KFF/CDC figure, but that is an outcome comparison, not a comparison of cohort group COMPOSITION to an external denominator, so I coded audits_selection_literal='no'. protected_attributes lists all attributes disaggregated in Table 2; the supporting quote names only the first three (age, sex, race/ethnicity) as the vocabulary limit of a single verbatim sentence. Missing values across all variables, including race/ethnicity (<5.8%), were mode-imputed.

title: Identify Patients at Risk of HIV Using a Clinical Large Language Model from Electronic Health Records.
venue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
notes: Strong filtering (>=1 year of EHR, 1 year continuous insurance enrollment, >=3 encounters) applied to a 20-million-patient source database down to 54,265, with no demographic accounting of the drop. The limitation sentence acknowledges the cohort is 'focused on people with access to care' but attaches no figure and makes no comparison to the OneFlorida+ parent composition or to Florida/CDC HIV surveillance figures, so audits_selection_literal = 'no'. null_attribute_handling coded 'separate_category' on the strength of the insurance variable, where unknown values are explicitly retained as an 'other/unknown' category (50.2% of the cohort, Table 1). Note the caveat: for the attributes actually used in the fairness stratification (sex, age, race/ethnicity) the paper never states how missing values were handled; race/ethnicity has an 'other' bucket (5.1%) that is retained in Table 1 but silently omitted from the Table 3 subgroup analysis, and 'sex: Other' (n=1) is likewise not analysed. A coder focused only on race/sex/age could reasonably code this 'unclear'. Insurance is disaggregated in Table 1 (by case status) but is not part of the fairness subgroup analysis.

title: FairCareNLP: An AI-driven patient review analyzer for healthcare.
notes: HARD CASE, and the weakest evidence base in the batch. Critical caveat: the dataset (>120,000 de-identified Ontario patient-experience reviews) contains NO patient demographics; the authors GENERATED synthetic gender/age/ethnicity/income labels by randomly assigning them to reviews in proportion to Statistics Canada / CIHI / Ontario Ministry of Health distributions, and admit the labels have 'little semantic alignment with the linguistic content of the reviews'. Every fairness number (EOD, WEAT) is therefore computed over fabricated group labels; I still coded audits_model_on_pool yes because equalized-odds disparities are reported per sensitive attribute (gender vs ethnicity vs income) on the analysis cohort, and null_attribute_handling as imputes because the whole protected attribute was absent and was inferred from population distributions. audits_selection strict coded no: the propensity-scoring module does test selection (Cramer's V for gender, age, ethnicity, income, employment, education, valence; 'those not in the labour force were underrepresented in the original online reviews') but the 'online reviewer' cohort being audited is a mock cohort the authors themselves synthesized from modified external distributions, and the paper's own analysis cohort filtering (null/duplicate removal, rows with unknown unit) is never audited. I coded the permissive field yes because there is an explicit statistical comparison of a reviewer cohort's demographic/socioeconomic composition against a different reference population's distribution with numbers attached. A stricter coder could code the permissive field no on the grounds that the compared population is synthetic.

title: Demographic prompt cues shift clinical recommendations in multimodal large language models: a multi-model audit of 25,380 dental radiograph assessments.
notes: HARD CASE for audits_selection, coded yes. The 'cohort' is 705 DENTEX benchmark radiographs with fictitious demographic labels; the filter that actually removes observations from the fairness analysis is GPT-5.4's 227 refusals, and the authors formally test whether that exclusion depends on the protected attribute (chi-square by race and by sex, both null) and additionally cross-tabulate refusals against image complexity and pathology, concluding the exclusion does not introduce systematic demographic bias. That is a statistical test of whether exclusion depended on a protected attribute, which the rules list as qualifying, so both strict and literal are yes - but note this audits an output-side filter, not selection of patients into a clinical cohort. cohort_is_filtered coded yes on the refusal-pair restriction plus the fact that the analysis pool is a pre-curated benchmark (all 705 annotated DENTEX training images; 27 zero-annotation images retained in primary analyses and dropped in a sensitivity analysis). null_attribute_handling coded separate_category because unstated demographics are analysed as their own experimental conditions (C1 'Not stated' and C2 blank), which is the designed analogue of a missing protected attribute rather than real-world missingness.

title: Demographic-aware temporal graph attention for fair and accurate cardiac abnormality detection in 12-lead ECG.
notes: HARD CASE for both selection fields, and the two are coded differently. Strict reading = no: the only thing resembling a composition check is the chi-square verification that the 70/15/15 patient-level split preserved class and demographic distributions, which is a randomisation/partition check rather than an audit of differential retention through a filter; the actual filter (21,837 -> 21,507 after dropping age>95 and low-SNR recordings) is reported only as a total count with no demographic breakdown. Permissive reading = yes: the paper repeatedly and explicitly compares its cohort's demographic composition to a specific external cohort figure (PTB-XL 47.5% male vs Chapman-Shaoxing 54.2% male, with age distributions), and discusses the European-to-East-Asian population difference at length. That is a comparison of the retained cohort's group composition to an external figure, which the permissive rule says counts, even though the referent is a second study dataset rather than a population denominator - flagging this as the main judgement call. Also note the paper is unusually explicit that it cannot audit race at all because neither dataset carries race/ethnicity metadata. null_attribute_handling = imputes, from the four-step deployment imputation cascade (population-mean age, s=0.5 for missing sex) plus a simulated-missingness degradation experiment.

title: Build fair machine learning models to predict adverse outcomes for heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction and with reduced ejection fraction.
notes: Cohort narrowed by ICD-based HFpEF/HFrEF phenotype algorithms, adult age, and one index hospitalization per patient; no flow counts of who was dropped and no demographic breakdown of exclusions, so audits_selection is no. The limitation that the single-health-system cohort 'may differ from nationally representative HF populations in demographics' is an unquantified representativeness caveat with no external figure, so audits_selection_literal is also no. 3.04% of patients have unknown race/ethnicity: this is reported in the cohort description but the paper never states whether unknown-race records were dropped, imputed, or retained in the FNR-parity contrasts (which are only Black-vs-White and Hispanic-vs-White), so reports_only. The abstract mentions age band as a fairness stratum but only sex and race/ethnicity results are reported; protected_attributes follows the Methods statement.

title: Disparities in AI-Based Prior Authorization for Head and Neck Reconstruction: A Large Language Model Analysis.
venue: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
notes: Synthetic vignette benchmark the authors constructed, so cohort_is_filtered = yes by the rules' note about author-constructed/sampled benchmark datasets: profiles are a hand-specified factorial grid (age 30 vs 60 only, four race/ethnicity levels, binary SES, ten hand-picked California zip codes). Borderline flag on audits_selection_literal: U.S. Census data IS cited, but it is used to CHOOSE the stimulus zip codes, not to compare the composition of the profile set against a population - so it does not qualify as a representativeness comparison, and I coded 'no'. There is no pre-selection population at all here, so a strict selection audit is not really applicable; coded 'no' rather than 'unclear' since the design is fully described. All demographic attributes are specified by construction, so protected-attribute missingness never arises and is never mentioned (searched: missing, unknown, not reported, declined, imputation, complete case - zero hits in the file).
